Alex — thanks for the detail and the attachment.

Quick summary of what Redwood can provide and next steps:

- Exportable artifacts: request-level telemetry (timestamped token/latency aggregates, anonymized request ids), runtime trace samples (inference kernel logs, memory/KV cache metrics), and periodic prefix/KV cache snapshots for dedicated tenants. We cannot export raw prompt/response content unless the customer explicitly consents because of PII/data residency concerns.
- Extraction windows: we support on-demand extraction for the last 7 days for hosted accounts; for Dedicated/Private customers we can provide 30/90 day snapshots depending on retention tier. For ephemeral traces older than configured retention we need the archive job (see runbook) which takes ~48–72 hours to build a consolidated extract.
- Handover options: secure SFTP or ephemeral signed GCS/Drive links with audit logs; for regulated audits we often do a live extraction with the auditor on the call to walk them through the artifacts.

I'm looping in Marissa and Jonas to confirm the extraction runbook and expected SLAs. Can we do a 30-minute call Wednesday 8/19 to finalize the sampling window and delivery mechanism? I'll prepare a short intake sheet that maps CAIQ control IDs to the artifacts we will hand off.

Best,

Irene Choi

Adding a couple of technical clarifications from the runtime side:

- For hosted tenants we keep high-resolution kernel traces for 72 hours; aggregated telemetry is retained for 90 days. If BlueMarble needs raw kernel trace slices beyond 72 hours we can run an archive job that reconstructs traces from aggregated telemetry and storage logs — that job is compute-intensive and we estimate a 48–72 hour turnaround.
- For Dedicated customers (reserved GPU pools) we can snapshot the KV cache and checkpoints directly from the instance; these are faster to extract (typically <24 hours) but require the customer's admin consent because they may include tenant-localized encryption keys or identifiers.
- We will redact any PII in extracts by default and provide a redaction report; if auditors need unredacted samples we will require a formal request and an approved NDA addendum.

I've attached the internal runbook excerpt that outlines the archive job steps and anonymization filters.

—Marissa

Attachment: runbook-log-extract.md
